findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. The check reads both files from the worktree at `ui_checks.py:60` and `:68`, while `close.py:276-280` selects the committed head and its changed paths. `worker.py:409-434` warns about remaining uncommitted work but does not stop close.
Case: normal use - A worker commits a drifting theme, corrects it locally, and leaves that correction uncommitted. Close compares the corrected worktree file and can publish the committed theme that still differs from the approved copy.
findings.title: Functional: Compare the committed theme and copy during close

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. Each later declaration replaces the previous declaration for the same name and theme, regardless of its selector.
Case: normal use - The root `--primary` differs from the copy, but a later component-specific rule sets `--primary` to the approved value. The later rule overwrites the root value in `found`, so close reports no drift even though screens outside that component use the differing root value. The same loss applies to other token families.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. This pattern only matches blocks whose bodies contain no nested braces, so it skips declarations belonging to a parent rule when that rule contains a nested rule.
Case: normal use - A developer adds a nested `@media` contrast adjustment inside the existing `.dark` rule. Close then treats the unchanged dark tokens in that rule as missing and refuses screen changes. Nested CSS is supported by the starter's [Tailwind tooling](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/compatibility#nesting).
findings.title: Functional: Preserve declarations in theme rules with nested CSS

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. Non-colour tokens get labels without a theme, so `--font-heading (light)` cannot match the waiver key. The shipped guide at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:869-882` requires a light or dark name in the comment and directs the agent to waive a font that cannot be loaded.
Case: normal use - An approved heading font cannot be loaded, so the agent keeps the app font and adds the documented `--font-heading (light)` waiver. Close still refuses the change and suggests a different comment that omits the required theme.
findings.title: Functional: Accept the documented waiver for shared theme values

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test. All the new-client drift cases reuse the screen branch started at line 75, including the copy edit at line 101. The test would still pass if close checked only screen changes and skipped theme-only changes. Lines 107-117 also never require both unwaived differences in one refusal or check a dark difference while the light value is waived, so reporting only the first mismatch or waiving both themes in that case can pass.
Case: normal use - An agent changes only the theme, or changes multiple values and waives one; this named proof does not establish that close reports the remaining differences.
